2,M,FRNFPIBLPO,40,Foreign,"Branch Office (BO), Liaison Office (LO), and Project Office (PO)",FRNBLPO,"None of these entities—Branch Office (BO), Liaison Office (LO), or Project Office (PO)—are allowed to invest in the Indian securities market.","C, F",R,"
NONE OF THESE ENTITIES (BRANCH OFFICE (BO), LIAISON OFFICE (LO), OR PROJECT OFFICE (PO)) ARE ALLOWED TO INVEST IN THE INDIAN SECURITIES MARKET.

A Branch Office (BO), Liaison Office (LO), and Project Office (PO) are all extensions of a foreign parent company operating in India under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and FEMA (Establishment in India of a Branch Office or a Liaison Office or a Project Office or any other Place of Business) Regulations, 2016. The difference lies entirely in what they are legally allowed to do:

Liaison Office (LO): This is strictly a non-commercial entity. Its purpose is to act as a communication channel between the foreign parent and Indian parties, conduct market research, or promote collaborations. A Liaison Office cannot earn any income or engage in trading. All its expenses must be funded by remittances sent from the parent company abroad.

Branch Office (BO): This is for ongoing commercial operations. A Branch Office is permitted to engage in specific business activities (like export/import, consultancy, or IT services) and can generate revenue in India. It is liable to pay Indian corporate taxes and can remit profits back to the parent company. (Note: If a foreign company operates as an RBI-licensed bank branch in India, select FRNBDCR and enable the Bank regulatory flag separately.)

Project Office (PO): This is a temporary setup designed specifically to execute a single, defined project (such as a large infrastructure, engineering, or construction contract awarded to the foreign company). It can earn income related to that specific project, but the office must be closed down once the project is completed.
